title: Beyond Perturbation Robustness: Do Genomic Foundation Models Learn Biological Equivalence?
conference: NeurIPS 2026 Women in Machine Learning (WiML) Workshop
description: Investigated whether genomic foundation models encode biological equivalence by testing whether synonymous DNA sequences are represented as more similar than matched nonsynonymous controls. Evaluated Omni-DNA, NucEL, and JEPA-DNA across translation-verified coding sequences, finding model-dependent biological-equivalence structure with NucEL showing the strongest signal.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Donor-Acceptor Coupling in SpliceBERT
description: Used causal interventions and activation patching to uncover how SpliceBERT represents long-range donor-acceptor dependencies in RNA splicing. Identified a four-role computation involving positional geometry, acceptor-local feature construction, cross-site information transfer, and downstream readout, while finding that the overall computation is distributed rather than captured by a sparse circuit.

title: States of Disarray
conference: Creative Activity and Research Day, University of San Francisco
description: Integrated geographic, demographic, and electoral data to create analysis-ready redistricting datasets for all 50 U.S. states. Presented how integrated geographic data and MCMC outlier analysis help detect and understand partisan gerrymandering in elections.

title: Nanoworld - Where Small is Big
description: A comprehensive review of nanotechnology and machine learning applications in dentistry, including emerging developments in dental diagnosis, treatment, and patient care.
